instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: Run_Modes owns a closed four-value runtime enum, keeps workflow overlays separate, forbids overlay-based authority widening, and requires children to inherit or narrow the parent ceiling.
atoms.title: Closed runtime-mode and overlay canon is explicit

atoms.statement: HTE separates provider reasoning from action authority: PM executes every tool call through permissions and FileSafe, and provider-originated tool use is terminally forbidden.
atoms.title: HTE keeps every real action host-owned

atoms.statement: DAE must execute in a PM-managed jail, treat actual jail diff as mutation truth, keep the canonical workspace non-writable, and reconcile only after scans and FileSafe checks.
atoms.title: DAE isolates canonical workspace writes

atoms.statement: Each DAE child receives its own jail, but this owner text does not define reconciliation ordering, conflict detection, atomic application, stale-base rejection, or rollback when sibling diffs touch the same canonical path.
atoms.title: Concurrent child-jail reconciliation has no merge transaction

atoms.statement: The selection algorithm is deterministic only for its declared snapshot; the document itself records that per-account DAE eligibility and child account re-resolution ordering are missing, and that mid-run account switches can invalidate committed strategy.
atoms.title: Per-account DAE eligibility and account-switch ordering are explicitly unresolved

atoms.statement: The caps and queue-on-full behavior are exact, but no fairness key, priority policy, cancellation semantics, durable queue identity, or crash/pause replay ordering is defined.
atoms.title: Concurrency queue ordering and recovery are unspecified

atoms.statement: Budgets are frozen for a run, survive pause/resume, distinguish nesting from tool rounds, and allow per-run or child narrowing without widening the policy ceiling.
atoms.title: Run-envelope budget inheritance is bounded

atoms.statement: The consumer contract distinguishes kill.* supervisor triggers from done.* terminal reasons, retires kill.task_timeout as a consumer alias, and keeps pre-request and post-response budget exhaustion distinct.
atoms.title: Pre-dispatch kill reasons and terminal outcomes are deliberately separated

atoms.statement: The plan owns a single signal fan-out, isolated process groups, platform-specific grace periods, idempotent shutdown, durable event flushing, and crash-marked startup recovery.
atoms.title: Process-group shutdown and crash recovery are strongly specified

atoms.statement: Durability-flush failure escalates to done.crashed, while user or parent cancellation remains done.cancelled even after forced termination; the simultaneous case has no stated precedence or multi-reason encoding.
atoms.title: Shutdown outcome precedence is not total

atoms.statement: Memory-pressure monitoring and controlled restart are mandatory, but threshold units, sampling window, sustained-growth definition, hysteresis, restart budget, and unhealthy-helper routing are not specified here.
atoms.title: Helper health monitoring has no measurable restart oracle

atoms.statement: The plan precisely defines executed-shell fingerprints, reset behavior, normalized file identity, qualifying mutations, sliding-window timing, and exclusions for denied, blocked, UI-only, no-diff, rollback, and PM-owned operations.

atoms.statement: All three scans are required before finalization, but their ordering, timeout/retry policy, snapshot identity, mutation freeze, and atomic relationship to reconciliation and terminal-event persistence are not defined.
atoms.title: Mandatory DAE scans lack a finalization transaction boundary

atoms.statement: Every run receives exactly one of seven coarse outcomes; transport status remains separate, explicit cancellation is not generic failure, and restart/replacement mints new identity.

atoms.statement: The jail is called ephemeral and security scans are mandatory, but retention, secure deletion, crash remnants, provider transcript redaction, diagnostic redaction, and recovery ownership for sensitive jailed content are not specified; the gap register separately admits jail-durability uncertainty.

atoms.statement: Ask and plan exclude mutation authority metadata, regular/yolo receive full execution context, and child, subagent, and rotated runs may only narrow the effective overlay.

atoms.statement: Ask and plan may use read-only repository, LSP, task, browser, and web evidence capabilities through normal permissions; denial remains visible with recovery instead of silently hiding the feature.

atoms.statement: The contract fixes precedence between six roots but does not order multiple matching paths inside the same `**` root. It also offers CWD-derived git root and selected project path as alternatives without defining which wins when they differ. First-wins can therefore vary by filesystem enumeration or caller entry point.
atoms.title: Discovery is not deterministic within one recursive root or between root-selection inputs

atoms.statement: The shared payload names `input`, while slash/NL routing names `arguments?`; no normalization, precedence, type, or serialization rule connects them. The skill-defined input schema is said to live in a manifest, but the only canonical file is SKILL.md and its frontmatter schema never names the input-schema field or dialect.
atoms.title: Invocation input has two unjoined field vocabularies and an undefined manifest schema slot

atoms.statement: The source defines timeout and permission-blocked outcomes but the result envelope has no invocation ID, success/error discriminator, error-code union, cancellation acknowledgement, retry/idempotency contract, or rule for suppressing a result that races timeout cancellation.
atoms.title: Invocation has no operation identity, terminal result union, or late-completion rule

atoms.statement: The document declares a complete five-value readiness vocabulary, separately defines five runtime-facing readiness values, and uses different source and projection enums in management, result, compatibility, and record contracts. In particular, `projected_in_sync` conflicts with `projected`, and `bundled` conflicts with `pm_bundled` without a normative translation table.
atoms.title: Readiness, source, and projection state vocabularies lack a canonical mapping

atoms.statement: Agent Config > Skills owns skill management; Settings owns system dependencies; Skill Store is install-only; management rows expose provenance, readiness, warnings, validation, permissions, and actions with dependency deep-links back to the owning Settings surfaces.
atoms.title: GUI ownership and management/store separation are explicit

atoms.statement: A Skill ID is the frontmatter `name`, and the folder must equal that ID, but Keep Both is specified only as a generated suffix. The contract does not say whether it rewrites `name`, directory, references, content hash, or provenance, nor how the suffix is chosen deterministically.
atoms.title: Keep Both collision handling conflicts with Skill ID and folder-name invariants

atoms.statement: Archive import explicitly rejects traversal, absolute paths, link escapes, case-normalized duplicate paths, deep nested archives, package-size overflow, and expanded-size overflow; case-only Skill ID collisions are rejected on every platform.
atoms.title: Archive import has concrete hostile-package limits

atoms.statement: The GUI requires badges, filters, links, technical IDs, remediation text, and issue-specific buttons, but the assigned core supplies no keyboard, focus, screen-reader, non-color, reduced-motion, truncation, pluralization, locale, or text-expansion behavior.
atoms.title: Dense skill-state UI has no accessibility or localization contract

atoms.statement: The acceptance section tests discovery order, duplicate shadowing visibility, and explicit-path roots. It provides no document-level oracles for invocation schemas/results, timeouts, permission recovery, readiness mappings, projection, child inheritance, imports, catalog flows, lifecycle races, or GUI remediation.
atoms.title: Document-level acceptance covers only three early behaviors

atoms.statement: The segment atomizes the prologue into accepted, non-executable PlanUnits for SSOT authority, Skill ID rules, SKILL.md frontmatter, verbatim body loading, project/global roots, and first-wins discovery, with exact tokens, source lineage, owner hints, and explicit no-WorkNode boundaries.
atoms.title: SS-002 through SS-007 preserve authority, identity, format, body, roots, and shadowing

atoms.statement: The standard PlanUnit template checks addressability, source-span preservation, and absence of executable artifacts, then names only migration/index validators. It does not state executable or falsifiable behavior-specific oracles for the unit's canonical_text.
atoms.title: Most PlanUnit acceptance criteria certify preservation rather than behavior

atoms.statement: This segment creates distinct accepted PlanUnits for invalid/shadowed GUI visibility, discovery validation, provider-agnostic registry resolution, invocation payload, safe result envelope, and runtime readiness/auto-invoke gating.
atoms.title: SS-008 through SS-013 split GUI invalidity, loader validation, registry, payload, result, and readiness

atoms.statement: The same file-tree/restore/revert negative constraint appears in the invocation payload, result-envelope, and readiness units even when their canonical_text does not own those flows. This creates apparent coverage without identifying the precise operation, state, or oracle that each unit must enforce.
atoms.title: Active-worktree constraint is mechanically copied into unrelated PlanUnits

atoms.statement: The segment preserves tool/Terminal authority, three converged invocation surfaces, one-SKILL.md delivery, provider-native non-goal, opt-in projection with copy-first portability, and visible projection/provenance state.
atoms.title: SS-014 through SS-019 preserve execution, invocation, package, provider, projection, and GUI boundaries

atoms.statement: The accepted canonical_text says the skill tool does not own shell/PTX execution, while the source contract and preserved token say PTY. PTX is undefined and breaks exact source fidelity in an authority-boundary requirement.
atoms.title: SS-014 canonical_text changes PTY to PTX

atoms.statement: Projection defines targets, states, copy/symlink defaults, drift, and portability, but not staging/atomic replacement, existing-target conflicts, permission failures, rollback after partial copy, symlink target revalidation, uninstall ownership, or whether user edits may be overwritten.
atoms.title: Projection lacks atomicity, overwrite, rollback, and destructive-action semantics

atoms.statement: The segment gives canonical Skill-ID grants to Permissions, raw-path/resource enforcement to FileSafe, parent ceilings to child runs, and management/remediation consumption to Agent Config, Settings, Personas, and FinalGUISpec.
atoms.title: SS-020 through SS-025 connect permission, FileSafe, child runs, and GUI consumers

atoms.statement: The child must receive an effective compatible subset below the parent ceiling, but the source does not define evaluation time, permission/registry snapshot identity, behavior after parent revocation or skill replacement, or treatment of an already-running child invocation.
atoms.title: Child-run skill inheritance has no snapshot or revocation propagation contract

atoms.statement: Skill grants apply to logical Skill IDs, resource disclosure is confined to allowed roots, underlying file operations still pass through FileSafe, global roots are canonicalized, and symlinked roots escaping the permitted set are rejected.
atoms.title: Skill permission never bypasses FileSafe and roots are canonicalized

atoms.statement: The segment separates GUI readiness taxonomy, persisted readiness records, package import UI, warning/NL routing, slash grammar, and OpenCode reference-only constraints into accepted PlanUnits.
atoms.title: SS-026 through SS-031 cover readiness records, import, runtime routing, and baseline deltas

atoms.statement: SS-029 includes user-visible natural-language examples and routing behavior but declares `gui_related: false`. Under the document's own classification rationale, chat invocation and visible discovery are user-facing surfaces and should not be silently classified as backend-only.
atoms.title: SS-029 is marked non-GUI despite owning natural-language chat behavior

atoms.statement: The source gives strong preconditions and size limits but does not require quarantine/staging, atomic commit, cleanup of partial extraction, revalidation after copy, behavior when validation fails after some skills import, or protection against link/path changes between validation and write.
atoms.title: Archive import rejection rules lack transactional cleanup and race handling

atoms.statement: The segment atomizes discovery-order, shadowing-GUI, and allowed-root acceptance, then adds concrete invocation timeout, permission-blocked, remediation-command, archive-limit, and collision oracles in SS-035.
atoms.title: SS-032 through SS-035 preserve the three original ACs and the FABLE residual contract

atoms.statement: The core range includes the retired SS-001 PlanUnit, Migration Coverage, and the start of a second FABLE addendum, while the segment's required-source roster identifies only SS-032 through SS-035. Those reviewed lines have no dedicated required source-unit identity, so attribution and downstream coverage credit are structurally ambiguous.
atoms.title: Final core segment contains unrepresented semantic content

atoms.statement: SS-035 fixes timeout units/default/max/event, blocked permission fields, canonical remediation command refs, archive limits, and collision outcomes, while explicitly prohibiting UI wiring, runtime certification, buildability proof, and executable/governance artifacts.
atoms.title: SS-035 closes exact timeout, permission, remediation, and archive fields without claiming runtime proof

atoms.statement: The contract recursively scans roots and preserves arbitrary Markdown bodies but specifies no maximum skill count, directory depth, file/body/frontmatter bytes, YAML alias expansion, scan deadline, cancellation, incremental index, or rescan backpressure. Archive limits do not cover already-present project/global skills.
atoms.title: Discovery and SKILL.md parsing have no scale or resource limits

atoms.statement: Invocation may carry active file, selection, conversation ID, content, resource samples, and arbitrary metadata, but the assigned core does not define minimization, user visibility, redaction, persistence, retention, deletion, telemetry exclusion, or provider disclosure for those fields.
atoms.title: Invocation context and output lack privacy lifecycle rules

atoms.statement: The source names a timeout event and dynamic roster updates but no invocation-start/success/failure/cancel events, registry revision, roster-change cause, correlation ID, duration, source hash, permission snapshot binding, audit retention, or support-facing diagnostic bundle.
atoms.title: Registry and invocation observability are incomplete

atoms.statement: Remote ad-hoc import is correctly excluded in favor of Catalog distribution, and catalog/GitHub origin URLs are displayed, but the source does not define offline browsing, cached metadata, interrupted install, retry/backoff, stale catalog state, link unavailability, or rollback after network loss.
atoms.title: Catalog and origin-linked flows have no offline or network-loss behavior
